note: Cases built from entities/entity_mutation.rs validate_orbital_entity_mutations: ORB_SHARED_ENTITY_FIELD_CONFLICT and ORB_SHARED_ENTITY_RENDER_AUTHORITY on [shared] entities (a render root is the trait that embeds the reader through `@trait.<Name>` in render-ui effects; two slots, a cycle and a nested render-ui control), and ORB_ENTITY_SPLIT_MUTATION on [runtime] entities (the consequence read, page-disjoint mutators, same-source-trait instances, a persistent entity and a lone mutator are the controls). The first three cases are resolved .orb programs whose expected findings are the ones the core checks report. The fourth case is the deliberate difference from Rust: a render-ui that only reads an `@intrinsic` field of the shared entity is not a render read of the shared row (the trait's own frame, never persisted), so In1 and In2 give no finding where Rust reports one, and In3, whose readers both name persisted fields, still fires. Its expectation is therefore the lint output, checked by hand to be exactly the In3 finding.

findings.suggestion: Keep a single trait's render-ui reading this shared entity into this slot; route the others through it, or give them a different slot
